title: Treesitter: syntax highlighting for command line, window
body:
### Problem

The command line does not have syntax highlighting, despite having a shiny new Vimscript parser at home. Also, enabling treesitter highlighting for vimscript breaks/disables the legacy parser for the command window (`q:`).

### Expected behavior

Hook a treesitter highlighter into the command line (and window) so we can have rainbow goodness (including highlighting of embedded Lua). This requires extending the `TSHighlighter` with a new mode that parses each line independently as its own tree (or writing a custom `TSLineHighlighter`).

This will also allow us to remove the custom (unmaintained) vimscript parser used for `<c-r>=` expression highlighting (although that will require some trickery to parse the whole line as Vim expression rather than statement).

comments.author: participant4
comments.body:
I've been poking around with this a little bit today, and I found that if you set `syntax=vim` in the cmdwin, you get what looks like Treesitter syntax highlighting. This seems like a similar issue to https://github.com/folke/noice.nvim/blob/92433164e2f7118d4122c7674c3834d9511722ba/lua/noice/text/syntax.lua#L12.   I made an autocommand for my config:

```lua
vim.api.nvim_create_autocmd('CmdwinEnter', {
  pattern = '[:>]',
  desc = 'If the treesitter vim parser is installed, set the syntax again to get highlighting in the command window',
  group = vim.api.nvim_create_augroup('cmdwin_syntax', {}),
  callback = function ()
    local is_loadable, _ = pcall(vim.treesitter.language.add, 'vim')
    if is_loadable then
      vim.cmd('set syntax=vim')
    end
  end
})
```

I'm going to keep digging into a less hacky patch for both of these

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
> to align on whether we actually prefer a C implementation over ext_cmdline.

No objection to a C impl if these are true (seems like "yes" based on your code snippet):

- it's more straightforward in the near-term (not tons of complicated code)
- it isn't a "one-way door" (shifting to a different approach in the future won't require disentangling fragile special-cases spread around the C codebase, or unwinding a public interface).

comments.author: participant6
comments.body:
> it's more straightforward in the near-term (not tons of complicated code)

Hard to say, beyond the snippets posted, some more trickery is needed to e.g. set the cursor position and expand the cmdline when it goes beyond the available Columns. Replacing(deleting) this in case we end up moving to a lua based cmdline in the future will require some work. So if that seems likely, I don't think having this as an intermediate solution makes sense.

> it isn't a "one-way door" (shifting to a different approach in the future won't require disentangling fragile special-cases spread around the C codebase, or unwinding a public interface).

I don't think it would be more spread out than it already is. The implementation just requires minor adjustments, I don't foresee the call sites changing. 

I had no intention of exposing a public interface, at least at first. My goal would be to make this a drop in replacement for the current cmdline, i.e. indistinguishable from what we have now except for highlighting. At least at first, the floating window config could always be exposed later (and would likely be compatible with a lua based impl as well).

But I don't think it's wort the effort if ext_cmdline is seen as the way forward, also for the TUI.

comments.body:
Hmm replacing the cmdline with a floating window is doable but quite cumbersome. The interactions with the current cmdline and the message grid (on which it is drawn) are quite involved and identifying/replacing all of them requires some work.

I wasn't aware before but while working on this I found out that we already have a way to color the command line lol. I now wonder if it will be more straightforward to just use a scratch buffer with the cmdline contents, attach treesitter (that part I have finished), extract the applied highlights, and still draw them on the message grid through `color_cmdline()`.

Though it seems the only way to do that is through the experimental `g:Nvim_color_cmdline`. If we can deprecate this color callback, along with the VimL/expression parser by replacing the cmdline with a colored floating window, and if that would be preferred, I can continue with resolving display issues. Any thoughts?

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
I'm not against that, mind you; especially if it's easier or more robust. We'll also have to consider that GUIs may still want to hijack `ext_cmdline`.

But we _do_ want to make `vim.ui_attach()` a first-class consumer of `ext_foo`, so if we can get rid of the need for hacks (in C), so much the better. This is not a trivial change and thus not part of the 0.10 milestone.
